stories.title: Cruz Hewitt Wins First ATP Match in Washington — 22 Years After Lleyton's DC Title
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Cruz Hewitt (AUS, 17, World No. 612) defeated Marcos Giron 6-3, 6-4 in 74 minutes in the first round of the Mubadala Citi DC Open on Tuesday July 28. It was Cruz's first ATP Tour match win. He became the youngest player to win a match in Washington since Kei Nishikori in 2007. His father, former world No. 1 Lleyton Hewitt, won the Washington title in 2004 — exactly 22 years before Cruz's breakthrough. Lleyton was courtside for the match. Cruz recently made the Wimbledon junior singles final (lost to Jordan Lee, USA). He is ranked No. 612 in the world. Note: July 28 TFR pipeline incorrectly placed Cruz Hewitt in Los Cabos (Story 4); his ATP debut and first win occurred at the DC Open in Washington.

stories.title: Eala Battles Back to Defeat Zheng — Advances to DC Open Round of 16
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Alexandra Eala (Philippines, career-high No. 29) defeated Qinwen Zheng (China, Olympic champion) 4-6, 6-4, 6-1 in the first round of the Mubadala Citi DC Open on Tuesday July 28. Eala dropped the first set before recovering to win 12 of the next 13 games and take the match. Zheng was notably cool in the post-match handshake. Eala advances to the Round of 16 where she faces No. 7 seed Leylah Fernandez (defending champion) on Wednesday.

stories.title: Venus Williams Loses Again; Fils Exits Hurt — DC Open Day 2 Round-Up
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Day 2 results at the Mubadala Citi DC Open produced two notable stories. Anastasia Potapova (RUS) defeated Venus Williams (USA) 6-3, 6-3 in straight sets on Tuesday. Williams drops to 0-9 in 2026 and has now lost 12 consecutive matches. Rafael Jodar (ESP) defeated No. 8 seed Arthur Fils (FRA) 7-6(5), 6-3 after Fils called for the physio in the second set for a recurring back and hip issue. Jodar advances to face Kei Nishikori. Jakub Mensik (7) beat Trevor Svajda 6-2, 6-7(5), 6-3 in a comeback win. Ben Shelton (2) advanced. Top seeds generally held.

stories.title: Shapovalov Wins Los Cabos Opener — Birthday Dedication as Defending Champion
stories.angle: NEW STORY — Denis Shapovalov (CAN, 8th seed, defending champion) defeated Rinky Hijikata (AUS) 2-6, 6-3, 6-2 in the first round of the Mifel Tennis Open by Telcel Oppo (ATP 250) in Los Cabos, Mexico on Wednesday July 29. Shapovalov is 5-0 all-time at Los Cabos and now holds the tournament record as its most successful player. This was only his second win since mid-April. Shapovalov dedicated the win to his wife, Mirjam Björklund, on her birthday.
